name: Kingdom of Spain

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 505,981 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 499,686 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2). Includes Balearic and Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla.

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 49,355,143). Low is the 2024 value; high allows for 2026 growth at the recent ~1%/yr immigration-driven rate. Everything inside ne:ESP incl. Canaries, Ceuta, Melilla.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 p.134 as quoted: 122,200 active (excludes 87,450 Guardia Civil paramilitary). CIA Factbook 2025 gives ~120,000; low/high span both. World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 199,000 (2020) includes paramilitary.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2025: 13,800 reserves. Low is the Army reserve figure 8,478 (2022, Spanish Army article citing Anuario Estadistico Militar). Spain has no conscript reserve; mobilization of 19-25 year olds is legally possible (CIA Factbook).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 122,200 (IISS 2025) minus infantry P roles (6,000 + 13,000). Covers navy (25,449 personnel 2025 per Spanish Navy article, minus the marine infantry counted under infantry_light), air force (26,953, 2025), armour/artillery crews, logistics, staff, UME.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to 20th-century Western European total-war mobilization (WWII belligerents reached roughly 8-15% of population); scaled down for an all-volunteer force with no conscript reserve and no stored equipment to arm mass levies. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Mechanized/armoured infantry personnel: roughly 10 mechanized battalions (BRI X, XI, XII, Canarias motorized) x ~550 infantry. Army strength 91,775 (2025) per Spanish Army article; the rest is crews, artillery, support. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Army)

quality.note: Rubric row quality 0.75 (among era best): Pizarro IFV, Dragon 8x8 entering service, but many M113/BMR still in use.

training.note: Rubric row training 0.75: professional standing army; NATO eFP rotations in Latvia/Slovakia.

count.note: Educated guess. Light, airborne (BRIPAC), Legion, mountain and marine infantry (~5,000 marines per Spanish Armed Forces article): ~24 battalions x ~500 plus marines. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Armed_Forces)

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band, slightly lower: light kit, VAMTAC/RG-31 mobility.

training.note: Rubric training 0.75-1.0: Legion and paratroopers are long-service professionals with Afghanistan/Iraq/Mali experience.

count.note: IISS Military Balance 2025 as quoted: 219 Leopard 2E + 55 Leopard 2A4 active; high adds 25 Leopard 2A4 in storage. Excludes 82 Centauro wheeled tank destroyers (counted nowhere; note for editors).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: Leopard 2E is a contemporary 2A6-class tank without active protection.

count.note: Sum of listed in-service figures: Pizarro 204 + Pizarro command 21 + Dragon 8x8 119 + M113 family 800 + BMR-600 648 + RG-31 150 + VEC-M1 135 = 2,077. Low allows for IISS counting fewer active M113/BMR.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 era-typical: fleet dominated by M113 and BMR (1970s-80s designs), Pizarro and Dragon modern.

count.note: M109A5E 96 + SBS 155/52 82 + L118 105mm 56 = 234 tubes >=105mm. No MLRS delivered yet (SILAM 0/12); K9 ordered (0/128 delivered). 120mm mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5 era-typical: M109A5E is old; no MLRS.

count.note: Air and Space Force inventory table: Eurofighter 70 + EF-18 Hornet (A+/M and B/BM) 81 = 151. Low allows for attrition and EF-18 retirements as Halcon Typhoons arrive.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: 4.5-generation Typhoon plus upgraded legacy Hornet; no 5th-generation aircraft.

training.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: NATO-standard flying hours, Baltic Air Policing rotations.

count.note: Navy AV-8B Harrier II: 12 EAV-8B + 1 TAV-8B (one EAV-8B lost 2024). Spain has no dedicated bombers; Typhoon/Hornet strike role counted under fighters.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: Harrier II Plus is an aging design.

count.note: Army 110 (Tiger 18, CH-47F 17, AS332 14, AS532 17, NH90 26, Bell 212 6, H135 12; World Air Forces 2025 as quoted) + Air Force 58 (NH90 12, AS332 10, AS532 2, S-76 8, EC120 15, H135 11; Air and Space Force article) + Navy 29 (NH90 4, SH-60B/F 18, H135 7; Spanish Navy article). Only 18 are attack helicopters.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: Tiger and NH90 modern, Bell 212/AS332 old.

count.note: Group 2+ UAVs only (hand-launched minis excluded): MQ-9A Block 5 4 (Air and Space Force) + Searcher Mk II/III 4 + Fulmar X 2 (Army list) + ScanEagle 8 (Navy) = 18. Excludes 72 RQ-11 Raven.
Convention used for all 2026 snapshots: ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates. Juan Carlos I LHD 1 + Alvaro de Bazan (F-100, Aegis) 5 + Santa Maria (F-80) 6 = 12.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: F-100 Aegis frigates among era best; F-80 are 1980s design.

count.note: Galicia-class LPD 2 + Meteoro (BAM) OPV 6 + other patrol vessels 15 + Segura MCM 6 = 29. Auxiliaries (18) excluded.
Active list: Galerna (Agosta) 1 + Isaac Peral (S-80 Plus) 1. High allows for the second S-80 (Narciso Monturiol) entering service during 2026.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: S-80 Plus with AIP is modern, Agosta is old.

training.note: Rubric 0.75 band minus: long gap with very few boats.

count.note: Batteries/fire units derived from launcher counts on the Army equipment list: Patriot 18 launchers ~3 batteries, NASAMS 8 launchers ~2, I-Hawk 32 launchers ~5, Oerlikon 35mm 92 guns with 18 Skyguard fire-control units ~18, Mistral 168 launchers / ~12 per battery ~14. Total ~42.

quality.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: Patriot/NASAMS modern, I-Hawk and Mistral 1 dated.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75 (trained staff system, proven commanders) slightly discounted: NATO-integrated staff, Spain hosts NATO CAOC Torrejon and a rapid deployable corps HQ (Valencia), but no large-scale combat command since 1939.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: professional force with strong unit identity (Legion, BRIPAC, marines).

morale.note: Rubric 0.5 average, slightly up for home defence: low public appetite for war abroad, high for defence of Ceuta/Melilla/Canaries.

weapons.note: Between anchor 9 (1985 guided missiles, MBTs with FCS) and 10: Meteor, IRIS-T, Taurus, Spike; few drones/loitering munitions, no hypersonics.

armor.note: Anchor 9 composite armour (Leopard 2E); no active protection systems fielded (anchor 10).

ships.note: Anchor 9 (Aegis) to 10: F-100 Aegis frigates, AIP S-80; F-110 frigates not yet in service; no networked USV fleet.

fortification.note: Anchor 9 hardened shelters; partial layered air defence (Patriot, NASAMS) short of anchor 10.

logistics.note: Anchor 9 containerised + airlift (14 A400M), NATO logistics integration; limited sealift.

communications.note: Anchor 9-10: SPAINSAT NG military satellites, Link 16, NATO C2.

isr.note: Anchor 9 satellites (PAZ radar satellite) plus a small MQ-9 fleet; short of persistent drone ISR (10).

air.note: Between anchor 9 (1985 jets) and 10 (5th generation): Typhoon is 4.5 generation, no F-35.

cyber.note: Anchor 10 state cyber forces partly met: Mando Conjunto del Ciberespacio (MCCE) exists; mid-tier capacity.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD 49,318.1 (2021 int$) x 0.8005 = 39,479 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 2,434,102,152,355 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,948,498,772,960 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 2.13% of GDP in 2025 (NATO 2% pledge reached), 1.46% in 2024, 1.37% in 2021. Low is 2024.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 19.6% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS); 21.2% in 2022.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.25 -> 0.95. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 3.37% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.63 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.55-0.74). Mid 1 - 0.034/0.63 = 0.95. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.55 = 0.91. High: s 0.74 = 0.95. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 63% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess: large net exporter of fruit, vegetables, olive oil and pork but imports feed grain; not computed from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 24,226,170 x share of males aged 15-19 5.647% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 273,589. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

armor.note: Educated guess: Leopard 2E line (Santa Barbara Sistemas) is closed; the Leopard 2A8 replacement is planned but not in production. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Spanish_Army)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess: Dragon 8x8 programme (348 first phase, 119 delivered) at Indra/Santa Barbara/Escribano; wartime surge could roughly double peacetime rate. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Spanish_Army)

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: Airbus Getafe is one of four Eurofighter final assembly lines (Halcon I/II orders); 1-2 per month at full rate with European supply chain. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Air_and_Space_Force)

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Navantia Ferrol builds F-110 frigates (first entering service ~2026-27); about one hull per year. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Navy)

roadKm.note: CIA World Factbook as quoted: 683,175 km roads, all paved (2020), incl. 17,228 km controlled-access highway. Low allows for definitional differences (municipal roads).

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 15,963 route-km (World Bank). CIA Factbook 15,489 km (2020). Mixed Iberian/standard gauge; standard-gauge high-speed network connects to France.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 52 ports, 3 large + 14 medium = 17; 17 key ports named (Algeciras-region, Barcelona, Valencia, Bilbao, Las Palmas...). Low counts only large ports plus main naval bases.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 1,601 thousand DWT under the Spanish flag (incl. Canary Islands special register). High is an educated guess for Spanish-owned tonnage under foreign flags.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess by analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment (truck-based, depots every ~150-200 km); Spain has limited deployable logistics and 14 A400M.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess for horses, mules and donkeys (not from FAO data). Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Spain is a non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS. No NATO nuclear sharing in Spain.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: familiar mountainous terrain (Meseta, Pyrenees, Cantabrian range), local supply, population support; no harsh-climate/deep-depth bonus.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 data with 2026 order of battle. Population convention: everything inside ne:ESP (peninsula, Balearics, Canaries, Ceuta, Melilla); World Bank figures. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Force counts from IISS Military Balance 2025 as quoted on Wikipedia, Wikipedia inventory tables (World Air Forces 2025), and the active-ships list; ships_major = carriers/LHD + cruisers + destroyers + frigates; ships_minor = LPD/LSD, corvettes, OPVs, patrol, MCM; drones = Group 2+ UAVs only. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). basesAbroad empty: Spain has no permanent overseas bases; ~3,000 troops deployed on EU/NATO/UN missions (CIA Factbook 2025). Guardia Civil (87,450) is paramilitary and excluded. US Naval Station Rota and Moron Air Base are on Spanish soil but belong to the US basing network.
